tasks.short: Note hours and materials, take photos and notes of work done, write the progress report, check it, send it to the site manager, and answer the site manager's questions.

steps.what: Carpenter maintains records of hours and materials on paper timesheets
Carpenter documents actions with photos and notes
Carpenter writes the written progress report

loop.input: The carpenter's voice note at the end of the day, the checklist items, hours and located photos.
loop.output: Filled checklist fields and a draft daily report.
loop.check: Code checks hours match the timesheet and every photo has a location; the carpenter confirms each field and the report.
loop.stop: One draft per day; fields the carpenter does not confirm stay empty.
loop.why_not_simpler: A voice note in site language must be sorted into checklist fields; a template cannot do that.

steps.what: Carpenter e-mails the report to the site manager
Carpenter answers the site manager's questions about progress by phone

tasks.design: Hours and materials go into the work order on the site app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) instead of a paper timesheet, and photos are taken in the app with location and checklist item, which also feeds the Wkb quality file. At day's end the carpenter speaks a voice note; a bounded step fills checklist fields and drafts the daily report, code checks hours and photo locations, and the carpenter confirms every field. Once checked, the report goes to the site manager, who sees photos and fields and phones less.
tasks.previous_blocker: Timesheets were paper, photos sat on personal phones and reports were typed at home.
tasks.enabler_now: Site apps capture hours, materials and located photos and export reports.
tasks.still_hard: Gloves, dust and rain make phone entry hard.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a detail was built differently from the drawing.
tasks.altitude: The carpenter confirms fields instead of writing reports.

reach.learn: Whether quality files are complete at handover.

evidence.claim: Syntess Atrium captures work orders, hours and materials on site.
At FAGSI, a project manager says PlanRadar saves about 10 hours a week on site diaries, defects and acceptance; self-reported, vendor-published.
Hours, location and job logs per worker need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from work done to questions answered; the quality assurer's review is outside.
Input contract: work orders in the site app; fallback is paper and typing.
The carpenter confirms every field and the report.
Photo locations are not used to track the carpenter.
research_questions: Do quality files reach handover complete more often?

already_counted.description: Carpenter confirms drafted fields and report.

incremental.description: Carpenter corrects voice-note errors in fields.

approvals.approved_version: The report as checked by the carpenter in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short jobs with few reports; high: long projects with daily reports and Wkb files.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study blueprints and specifications, take off dimensions and compute material quantities, mark out the layout on site, write the material list, and send it to the foreman.

steps.what: Carpenter studies specifications in blueprints, sketches or building plans
Carpenter determines dimensions and materials required by hand
Carpenter prepares the project layout on site
Carpenter hands the material list to the foreman

tasks.design: Dimensions and quantities are taken off the drawing in a takeoff tool on the tablet ({OTHER}) that measures from the PDF or model and computes boards, sheets and fixings, instead of scaling and adding up by hand. The material list is built from that takeoff in the site app, and once the carpenter has written it, it goes to the foreman for ordering. Reading the drawings and marking out on site stay with the carpenter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quantities were scaled from paper drawings and added up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Takeoff tools measure from PDF drawings and models on a tablet.
tasks.still_hard: Drawings and the site often differ.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a detail on the drawing cannot be built as drawn.

reach.learn: Whether orders arrive complete the first time.

evidence.claim: Takeoff tools can measure lengths and areas from PDF drawings and models.
Syntess Atrium supports material ordering and call-off for installation firms.

assumptions: Boundary: from building plans to the list with the foreman; ordering is outside.
Input contract: drawings as PDF or model from the architect; fallback is paper drawings.
Reading drawings and marking out do not change.
The foreman orders from the app as from paper lists.
research_questions: Do material shortages on site fall?

incremental.description: Carpenter checks takeoff scales against a known dimension.

approvals.approved_version: The material list as written by the carpenter in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small repairs; high: new builds with many drawings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The carpenter keeps reading drawings, marking out and building; paper timesheets, typed reports and hand takeoffs shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the site app and takeoff tool
role.ambitious_version: A carpenter with more time on the tools.
